From Surya, it was received by Manu, and from Manu, it reached Ikshvaku.

You gave this Yoga to Surya? But O Keshava, you have taken birth in this modern age, while Surya Dev is ancient. How can I believe that you imparted this Yoga to Surya Dev at the very beginning of creation? Please explain, Keshava.

Oh Partha, many births have passed for both you and Me. I remember them all, but you do not, O scorcher of foes. बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन। तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परंतप॥ Though I am unborn, imperishable, and the Lord of all beings, I appear through My own Yogamaya, subduing My own nature. Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and a rise of unrighteousness, O Bharata, then I manifest Myself. यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥ परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्। धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे॥ For the protection of the good, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the establishment of righteousness, I am born in every age. Thus, I manifest; I come whenever there is a decline of Dharma; I come whenever unrighteousness prevails. I come to protect the virtuous, to annihilate the wicked, to establish Dharma, and I take birth age after age.
But O Keshava, why does Dharma decline?

Dharma declines, Partha, because humanity fails to break the bondage of attachment. They sever their connection with their true self and thus cannot connect with society. O Partha, if this were not so, the Lacquer House incident would not have occurred, Draupadi's disrobing would not have happened, and the Kaurava and Pandava armies would not be standing arrayed against each other today.
Then, O Keshava, should I not have felt anger at Draupadi's disrobing?

That decision, Partha, you must make yourself. However, Draupadi's disrobing is not merely your personal problem. A society that remains silent during the public humiliation of Draupadi – the Empress of Indraprastha, daughter of King Drupada, and wife of the Pandavas – how can that society protect the honor of an ordinary woman? Draupadi's disrobing is a societal problem, Partha. It is a social problem, and it is your duty to wage war to destroy those powers that could disrobe any Draupadi. These are the powers of society...
Keshav, I still do not understand what benefit this war will bring.

Dhananjaya, gain and loss are both relative terms. I know that you do not desire earthly enjoyments or heavenly pleasures. Therefore, O Son of Kunti, treating alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, engage in battle; thus you will not incur sin. Rise above pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, Partha. सुख दुखे समय कृत्वा लाभा लाभ जया जय ततो युद्ध नवम पापम अवाप
Keshav, I am still unable to rise above these dualities.

Partha, until now, I was explaining to you from the perspective of knowledge and discriminative wisdom, which can see through life and understand the voice of its innermost self by peering into the depths of truth. But perhaps you got entangled in its abstractness. So, weigh this moment in the balance of practical action, Partha. From the perspective of practical action, decide about your duty; even then, you will arrive at the same conclusion that it is necessary for you to participate in this war.
Keshav, this is precisely the decision I am unable to make. I cannot make it.

Partha, you are unable to make this decision only because you are weighing this moment solely in the balance of personal gain and personal loss. This is indeed the bond of attachment, Partha; this is the root of your sorrow, and hence your cowardice. Do not waver, Partha. Simply perform your duty. Action (Karma) itself is virtuous, sacred, and beneficial for society. Action is its own fruit, Partha. But if you yourself engage in acts for the welfare of society...

O Keshav, if there are two paths—Jnana Yoga (the path of knowledge) and Karma Yoga (the path of action)—and Jnana Yoga involves looking within to find the Divine, why should I not simply follow the path of knowledge and thus be free from the burden of external action?

O Partha, Jnana Yoga is not a path for the abandonment of action, nor is it the way to perfection by renouncing karma, for life itself is impossible without action. Your eyes will certainly see, your eyelids will certainly blink, your ears will certainly hear. One who forcibly restrains their organs of action, yet continually dwells in the mind on the objects of the senses, is not a yogi or a man of knowledge; he is a hypocrite. An accomplished person controls their senses, but does not suppress them, O Partha. They do not live with closed eyes. Without action, even the journey of the body is impossible. Will a person not breathe, O Partha? If there is a fragrance or foul odor in the atmosphere, one is compelled to experience it. If there is a sound, a noise, or clamor nearby, their ears will not wait for their command to hear it. Therefore, he who keeps his senses controlled, who directs them towards action by placing the restraint of his consciousness upon them, showing them the direction of duty, is superior. He understands his options, O Partha, and uses his power of resolve. And, O Partha, performing your prescribed duties is better than inaction.

If action is indeed so indispensable, O Krishna, how then should a wise person act? What is the distinction in the actions of a knower and an ignorant one, especially since the senses are naturally inclined to their objects?

It is also true, O Partha, that eyes see, but a wise person himself decides what to see and what not to see. He does not give free rein to his eyes for seeing, his ears for hearing, or his feet for walking. At the point of choice, O Partha, the distinction between the wise and the ignorant becomes clear. Therefore, action is necessary, for without it, the sustenance of the body is impossible. However, O Partha, act like a wise person, perform your prescribed duties:
नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः। शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः।।
यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः। तदर्थं कर्म कौंतेय मुक्तसंगः समाचर।।
Meaning, O Son of Kunti, perform your actions as a Yajna (sacrifice), for karma itself is Yajna, and its source is the imperishable Brahma. Therefore, the path of action directly leads to Brahma. And for this reason, the person who does not contribute to running the cycle of creation, their life becomes valueless. Do not go towards this worthlessness, O Partha. Do not go towards this worthlessness. A person who only thinks about their own problems is a sinner. Therefore, break free from this net of delusion, recognize your duties, O Partha, and fulfill them. O Partha, the desire for the fruits of action is indeed an obstacle on the path.

O Lotus-Eyed Lord, my eyes have truly opened, and the clouds of doubt and apprehension have dispersed. All that You have revealed is the ultimate truth, and there is no truth beyond it. However, O Supreme Lord, I yearn to behold Your divine, all-encompassing form. How may I perceive it?

O sinless Arjuna, you cannot behold that form of Mine with these mortal eyes. For this, you will require divine vision. Therefore, I grant you divine sight. Behold My supreme yogic power! न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा। दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्॥

O Lord, having seen this form never seen before, I am filled with joy, yet my mind is also deeply disturbed by fear. Therefore, O Lord of gods, O Abode of the Universe, be pleased with me and reveal Your benevolent human form once more! Forgive me, O Lord, forgive me! O Vishwamurti, O Ananta, O Narayana, O Ocean of Mercy! Just as a friend forgives a friend, a father his son, and the Lord His devotee, so too, please forgive me, my Lord!

O son of Kunti, there is no place for forgiveness between a friend and a friend, a father and a son, or between the Lord and His devotee. The very foundation of these relationships is affection, faith, and devotion. One who fixes his mind on Me, constantly engaged in My worship with supreme faith, is considered the most excellent yogi. Therefore, O Partha, My devotion is supreme. Those who are My devotees do not become entangled in this world. मय्यावेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते। श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः॥
O Lord, Your words about devotion being the path to liberation from this world are profound. What then, is the true nature of this world, or Samsara, from which Your devotees are freed?

For, O Partha, this world is indeed like an eternal Ashwattha tree (fig tree), whose roots are above and branches below. Its leaves are the Vedas; he who truly comprehends this, understands the meaning of the Vedas. Its branches extend upwards and downwards, nourished by the three Gunas—Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Its roots are deeply embedded in human society, spreading far and wide. The true form of this tree cannot be perceived in this world, O Partha, for no one can truly discern its beginning, end, or foundation. ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्। छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्॥
My heart is filled with anguish, Krishna! How can I fight against my own kinsmen and revered elders? They stand before me as enemies, but my attachments prevent me from acting.

O Partha, cast aside your personal anger and attachment. Fight for the welfare of the world; this is your supreme duty. Do not hesitate to engage in battle even against those great men who have sided with these opposing forces. Observe Me, Partha; I have created this society and its divisions based on qualities and actions, yet I have never desired the fruits of this creation. Therefore, even while being the doer (karta), I am a non-doer (akata). One who understands this secret, Partha, will never be entangled by their actions.न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते।।Actions do not cling to Me, nor do I have any desire for the fruits of action. One who understands this truth about Me is also not bound by karmic reactions. I have no desire for the fruits of action, which is why actions do not contaminate Me. You too, Partha, perform actions without attachment to their results (Nishkam Karma), and do not let the shadow of your selfish interests fall upon your deeds.
O Keshav, what is the difference between Karma, Akarma, and Vikarma? Please enlighten me, for I am confused about these distinctions.

Listen, O Bharata, and understand the difference between Karma, Akarma, and Vikarma. Karma is simply action. However, that action which is performed without the expectation of its fruits is Akarma. And that which is not beneficial for the individual or society is Vikarma – it is forbidden. Karma is superior to Akarma, and a doer (karta) is superior to a non-doer (akata). O Partha, he who is a non-doer, free from the desire for the fruits of action, is truly wise, intelligent, and a Karmayogi. For him, his action itself is the fruit of action, and therefore, after performing one action, he does not wait for its result, but moves on to the next. The fire of his knowledge burns away the impurities of attachment, anger, hatred, ambition, gain and loss, joy and sorrow, purifying his actions. His actions then become Akarma, and he transforms from a doer to a non-doer. This non-doer, this wise one, does nothing for himself beyond securing the essential necessities of life. All his remaining actions are for the welfare of society. Such a person, even while performing actions, is not tainted by sin; his life itself becomes beneficial for society. O sinless Arjuna, the life of such a person is a Yagya (sacrifice). You too should make your life a Yagya, and in its sacrificial fire, burn your desire for the fruits of action, attachment, and anger like offerings.
And what is Yagya, O Keshav? Different people define Yagya in different ways, which further adds to my confusion.

O Partha, indeed, people define Yagya differently. For some, Yagya is the manifestation of Brahman; for them, everything is Brahman. Some perform Yagya to please the gods, and for them, worship is Yagya. Some seekers call the practice of uniting the individual soul with the Supreme Soul as Yagya. Like these Yagyas, the offerings made in them are also of different kinds; some offer wealth, while others offer actions. But in reality, Yagya is of four types. The first is Dravya Yagya, in which acquired wealth and resources are utilized for the welfare of society.

Keshav, I am filled with doubt regarding these paths. You speak highly of both the renunciation of action (Karma Sanyas) and the path of action (Karma Yoga). How can these two seemingly contradictory paths both be praised? And what becomes of those consumed by doubt?

Arjuna, those who are filled with doubt and indecision are indeed ruined, finding happiness neither in this world nor the next. Therefore, abandon all doubt, O Bharata, awaken the sage within you, and become a Yogi of Knowledge, Partha! Understand that the pinnacle of knowledge is indeed the renunciation of action. However, these two, Karma Sanyas and Karma Yoga, do not contradict each other; both are beneficial. Yet, among them, Karma Yoga is superior. One who performs actions without hatred or desire is a perpetual sannyasi, free from all dualities and liberated from worldly bonds. Therefore, one who considers Karma Sanyas separate from Karma Yoga is indeed foolish; the wise never make such a distinction. Renunciation of action, Partha, is truly the renunciation of self-interest. Thus, without Karma Yoga, the attainment of Karma Sanyas is impossible. A Karma Yogi possesses knowledge of the elements, and their every action—seeing or not seeing, hearing or not hearing, tasting or not tasting, waking or not waking, taking or not taking, abandoning or not abandoning—is for the welfare of the world. Therefore, they remain untouched by sin, just as a lotus leaf remains unaffected by water.

ब्रह्मण्याधाय कर्माणि सङ्गं त्यक्त्वा करोति यः।
लिप्यते न स पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवाम्भसा॥

O Dhananjaya, a Karma Yogi, by renouncing the fruits of action, attains the Supreme Power and dwells happily in the body, the nine-gated city.

Lord, you speak of this mortal life and the importance of knowledge. What causes humans to be deluded, and how does this knowledge liberate us in this very life, freeing us from the cycle of birth and death?

The reason for human delusion, Partha, is that ignorance covers their knowledge. But when self-knowledge destroys this ignorance, then knowledge illuminates that Supreme Truth like the sun. The wise attain the Supreme Truth in this very mortal life; they do not have to take birth again and again; they achieve liberation in this transient existence. Therefore, O Partha, this mortal life is exceedingly important, because after it, your soul will certainly exist, but 'you' as you know yourself will not. So, make this fleeting lifespan meaningful and beneficial for society, Partha. Knowledge is light; attain this light. If you do so, you will be saved from wandering in the delusions that plague you today.
If I am saved from these delusions, Krishna, will I then find peace? What is the direct path to peace, and how can I achieve it amidst this turmoil?

Indeed, Partha, if you are saved from wandering in delusion, you will find peace. O Dhananjaya, I am the direct path to peace. Those who know Me as the goal of every sacrifice, the Lord of every realm, and the benevolent friend of every being—only they attain peace. If you consider Me your well-wisher, Partha, then heed My words and fight! For without engaging in this battle, you cannot attain peace. The path of fleeing your Dharma is not the path to attaining peace, Partha. This war is your sacred duty. Therefore, fulfill your Dharma, Partha.

O Krishna, you are the Supreme Brahman, the Ultimate Purifier, the Eternal, the Divine Knowledge. O Lord of Yoga, O Embodiment of Wisdom, how can I know You? How can I recognize You? Please explain in detail, O Madhava, O Foremost Guru.

My manifestations are endless, yet listen. I am strength, and in beings, I am the desire that is not contrary to Dharma. I am in everyone, Arjuna, yet separate from all. I am imperishable; I am without attributes. O Arjuna, I know all beings of all past times, this present modern time, and all future times, but no one knows Me. I am indeed the father and the sustainer of the universe. I am the Rig Veda and I am the Sama Veda. I am the master and I am the refuge. I am creation and I am dissolution. I am the foundation of all, Arjuna; I am everything, everything. I am summer and I am rain, O Partha, and I am the imperishable seed of the universe. I am a most dear friend to all, yet I am the same to all. No one is dear to Me, nor disliked. But those who worship Me with faith, friend, they are in Me, and I am in them. समोऽहं सर्वभूतेषु न मे द्वेष्योऽस्ति न प्रियः। ये भजन्ति तु मां भक्त्या मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम्॥ I am the Self, seated in the hearts of all creatures. अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः। अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च॥ O Guḍākeśa, I am the beginning, the middle, and also the final end. Among the Ādityas, I am Vishnu. Among the Maruts, I am Marīci. Among the luminaries, I am the sun, and among the constellations, the moon. वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानां अस्मि वासवः। इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना॥ Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among the Yakshas and Rakshasas, I am Kubera. Among the Vasus, I am Agni, and among the mountains, I am Sumeru. Among priests, I am Brihaspati; among commanders, Kārtikeya, and among reservoirs, the great ocean. Among the great sages, I am Bhrigu; among words, Omkāra; among sacrifices, Japa Yajña; and among the immovable, the Himalayas. Among trees, I am the Peepal; and among the divine sages, Nārada. Among the Gandharvas, I am Chitraratha; and among the Siddhas, Kapil Muni. O mighty warrior, among horses, I am Uchchaihshravas, born from the nectar. Among elephants, I am Airavata, and among men, the king. Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, Kamadhenu; among progenitors, Kamadeva; and among serpents, Shesha Nāga. प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम्। मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्॥ Among the wielder of weapons, I am Rāma; and among letters, the syllable 'A'. I am inexhaustible Time. I am the four-faced creator, Arjuna. I am death, Arjuna, and I am the beginning of all those who are to be born in future times and whose beginning has not yet begun.

O Krishna, what truly hinders a person from rising above their own layers of self and fulfilling their higher purpose? How can one avoid being entangled in the mire of personal gain and loss, especially when facing such a momentous duty?

The stone tied around a person's neck that prevents them from rising above their own layers is precisely what cuts them off from society and pushes them into the mire of individual gain and loss. Society is not within you, Partha; you are in society. Therefore, consider Lok Sangrah (welfare of the people) and Lok Kalyan (public good) as your supreme duty. For what is beneficial for society will also be beneficial for you. The action performed for the welfare of the world, Partha, will grant you success (siddhi). The path of individual gain only leads to sin, as it misleads a person for self-gratification. And, O Partha, do not forget that you are a great man, and people will follow you as an example on the path of desire and self-interest, because the conduct of a superior person indeed becomes an example for others. Take Me, for instance: नमे पार्था कर्तव्यम त्रिश लोकेश किंचन नानत अत व्यम वर्त एव चकर मणि. In the three worlds, there is nothing that I need to do, nor is there anything unachieved that I need to achieve. Yet, I am before you, performing actions, O Partha, performing actions. I am demonstrating and proving that it is possible to live a life while walking the path of Nishkama Karma (disinterested action). सक्ता कर्मण्य विद्वान सो यथा कुर्वंति भारत कुर्यात विद्वान तथा सक्त चिकर शुर लोक संग्रह. O Bharata, even the ignorant perform actions, but only from the perspective of their vested self-interest. The actions of the wise are selfless; they are for maintaining the balance of the world, for public welfare. Therefore, O Partha, do not bear any burden on your mind. Offer your actions to Me and fight this righteous war. On the path of duty, even death becomes auspicious. If you have to slay Pitamaha, revered teachers, and relatives, you will still not incur sin, because the performance of duty is free from sin, Partha, the performance of duty is free from sin. If they attain a heroic death (Veer Gati), their death will be auspicious. And if you attain a heroic death, your death too will be auspicious. Therefore, O Partha, fight this war, because the path of Dharma cannot be the path of sin.
Since the topic of sin has arisen, please tell me, Keshav, why does a human sometimes become so compelled to commit sin? What compels them?

What compels them is their desire (Vasana); what compels them is their vested self-interest. Their anger (Krodh) and their attachment (Moh) make them commit sin. Recognize these enemies, Partha. Just as smoke covers fire, or dust covers a mirror, or a membrane covers an embryo, so do desire (Kama), attachment (Moh), and sensual desire (Vasana) cover knowledge. आवत जन मेते ज्ञानो नित्य वैरीना काम रूपेण कौंतेय दुष्प रेणा नले नच. This knowledge is covered by this eternal enemy of the wise, O son of Kunti, in the form of desire, which is insatiable like fire. The fire of desire (Kama) and attachment (Moh) destroys knowledge, and that is why it is the enemy of the wise, O Kaunteya.

O Krishna, my mind is bewildered by these conflicting duties. What is the ultimate path to liberation, and how can I truly free myself from sorrow and attain that supreme state from which one never returns?

O Partha, one can achieve that supreme abode, from which one never returns, by cutting down this tree of material existence with the axe of detachment. Detachment, my dear Partha, is the renunciation of inherent self-interest. Therefore, if you wish to think, think only of Me. If you wish to worship, worship only Me. Surrender yourself completely to Me, O best of archers. Come into My refuge, and I shall free you from all sin. I have told you:

मनमना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु। मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे॥
सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज। अहं त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचः॥

Fix your mind on Me, O Partha, become My devotee, and offer obeisance to Me. If you do this, I promise you truly that you will attain Me completely, for you are very dear to Me. Abandon all varieties of duties and simply surrender unto Me, O Partha. I shall deliver you from all sinful reactions; do not grieve, O Dhananjaya, do not grieve. O beloved one, O devotee, I am the culmination and supreme goal of Karma Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, and Jnana Yoga. Therefore, act like a Yogi, performing selfless actions. Do not worry, O Partha, do not worry! Have faith in Me, O mighty-armed one. Pick up your weapons and fight!
Lord Krishna, what should be my approach to this war, given the moral dilemmas and the potential outcomes? How do I reconcile my duty with detachment?

Do not think about the outcome, about who will live or die; that is not your concern. O son of Pandu, consider what people call 'Sannyasa' to be 'Yoga'. Fight free from doubt, hatred, and desire, for without abandoning these, no one can truly be a yogi.
How can one truly achieve self-mastery and uplift oneself? What is the relationship between the self, the mind, and the senses?

उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत्। आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः॥ A person must uplift themselves and not allow themselves to degrade. A person is their own friend and their own enemy. One who has controlled their ego, mind, and senses is their own friend, but he who is enslaved by them, O Partha, is his own enemy. A person who remains calm and balanced in winter and summer, in joy and sorrow, honor and dishonor, such a self-controlled person is always absorbed in the Supreme Self.
What practices or lifestyles are conducive or detrimental to achieving this state of Yoga, and how can I control my restless mind, which seems to constantly pull me in different directions?

However, O Partha, this Yoga is not attained by one who eats too much, or eats nothing at all, nor by one who sleeps too much, or sleeps too little. Life is about balance, O Partha, and the Yoga of a person who lives in a balanced way dispels all their sorrows. Just as the flame of a lamp remains steady in a windless place, so too does a yogi free from delusion remain steady. Do not let your fickle mind act on its whims, O Partha; restrain it and bring it under the control of your soul. This is the remedy for your confusions.
How can I overcome distraction and truly connect with the divine, or with you, Krishna? What happens to one who remembers you always? And who is considered the most superior among yogis?

Look towards me, O Partha, look towards me. One who sees only Me in every direction and in every object can never go astray. One who does not forget Me, O Partha, I also do not forget them. Even while leading a worldly life, such a one remains separate from the world and resides within Me. O Arjuna, the yogi who considers the happiness and sorrow of all as their own happiness and sorrow is truly supreme. आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन। सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः॥
But on the path of Yoga, the mind can surely wander, can it not, Keshav?
It can indeed wander, why not? It can certainly wander, Keshav!
What then is the consequence of this wandering on the path to realizing Brahman? Does the wanderer get scattered and lost like a fragmented cloud, Keshav?

One who wanders does not get scattered and lost like a fragmented cloud, Keshav. Whether in this world or the next, those who perform auspicious, meritorious deeds never meet a bad end. O son of Kunti, fix your mind on Me, practice Yoga depending on Me, and you will attain My doubtless, complete knowledge.
What is your true nature, Lord Krishna? What is the greatest truth?

O Dhananjaya, the greatest truth is Me alone. I am the thread on which all this creation is strung like pearls. O son of Kunti, I am the taste in water, the light in the sun and moon, the Omkara in the Vedas, and the sound in the sky. I am the sacred fragrance in the earth, the brilliance in fire, the life force in all beings, and the austerity in ascetics. O Partha, I am the primordial seed, the intelligence of the intelligent, the splendor of the splendid, and the strength of the strong, devoid of attachment and desire.

O Keshava, you speak of profound truths. I observe the ways of men, driven by desires and seeking worldly comforts. What is the nature of a true sage, a Muni, and how does he perceive this world differently? What truly constitutes supreme wisdom, and how does one attain it amidst all these worldly distractions?

Arjuna, consider the difference between a common man and a sage (Muni). A common man, for self-preservation against the seasons, desires a home; his thinking is self-centered. But the Muni, the Sthitaprajna, possesses objective insight. He sees beyond personal hunger and desire. He doesn't merely think about a fallen fruit; he contemplates the tree, the entire forest. If a common man needs wood for fuel, he will cut trees until the forest is destroyed. However, the Muni considers the importance of forests in nature, the balance of nature, and the relationship between forests and seasons. Therefore, O Partha, what is 'day' for the senses of the common man is 'night' for the Muni, for he has transcended the limits of the senses. And what is 'night' for the common man's senses is 'day' for the Muni, because it is in that silence that the sun of the Muni's consciousness rises. The Muni's interest lies not only in the immediate problems but also in their solutions, and this is what distinguishes him from the common man.या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी। यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुने॥What is night for all beings, therein the self-controlled one remains awake; and in that where all beings are awake, that is night for the introspective sage.O Partha, the truth is beyond the reach of the senses. It's not that a Muni doesn't feel hunger; he does. But he sees beyond his hunger and contemplates its remedy. Hence, the day of the common man is night for the Muni, and he who protects himself from this 'night' of the common man is truly a Sthitaprajna. The common man is like rivers, swept away by restlessness, unaware of their true path. They flow blindly, believing that merely flowing is their duty, pouring all their water and turbulence into the ocean. Yet, the ocean never violates the boundaries of its shores. Similarly, rivers of desires sweep away the common man, but when they reach the Muni, he absorbs them without violating his own dignity. O Partha, you too become an ocean. The ocean is a Muni, the ocean is wise. You too become wise, Partha, because knowledge is supreme.

O Hrishikesha, O Yogeshwara, O Janamurti! If knowledge is indeed superior to action, Keshava, why then are you urging me towards this dreadful, bloody action? Keshava, you have utterly confused me! If knowledge is superior to action, why should I engage in this terrible deed? Why should I fight? Keshava, why should I not simply become a Muni and retreat into silent meditation? I seek the path to ultimate welfare, Keshava; please, show me the way!

O sinless Arjuna, in this world, I have previously declared a two-fold path: the path of knowledge for the Sankhyas, and the path of action for the Yogis.लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ। ज्ञानयोगेन सांख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्॥O sinless one, in this world, a two-fold path was declared by Me of yore: the path of knowledge for the Sankhyas, and the path of action for the Yogis.There are two types of people in this world: the introverted and the extroverted. Those who are introverted, they...

O Krishna, I am perplexed by the myriad paths of action and spiritual discipline. What are the different forms of sacrifice, and which among them is the highest, leading to true welfare and liberation?

Listen, O Pārtha, there are various forms of Yajna (sacrifice). One is 'Lok Seva Yajna,' the sacrifice of service to humanity. Another is 'Tapo Yajna,' where one makes their own work a discipline; such a life becomes a penance and a sacrifice. The observance of your Dharma is also a sacrifice, but this Dharma is not sectarian; it is Sanātana, beneficial for both the individual and society. The third is 'Yoga Yajna,' which involves the practice of Ashtanga Yoga, where people embrace the path of meditation and samādhi, offering life energies into life energies.However, O Pārtha, the fourth is 'Jnana Yajna,' the sacrifice of knowledge. Although all four sacrifices are important, the greatest is 'Jnana Yajna,' for knowledge alone distinguishes between good and bad, and purifies actions in its fire, making them auspicious. Knowledge is the pinnacle of action's excellence, and knowledge alone will free you from the bonds of delusion. O Pārtha, only the boat of knowledge can cross the ocean of sin. You must act with knowledge, for the best knowledge is Dharma Karma Yoga; Dharma is Yoga, and Yoga is action.O human, I tell you that this world is your field of action, and you shall be measured by the standards of your actions. Therefore, do not strive to flee from actions, for your desireless action (Nishkama Karma) is your duty, and your duty is your Dharma. However, if your action is solely for your own benefit, it is a path leading to sin. Therefore, act for the welfare of society, free from self-interest, for this is the path to liberation. All other actions are captives of attachment, illusion, and anger; and those who are themselves captive, how can they lead you to the path of liberation? If society is not happy, the individual cannot be happy either. If there are tears in society's eyes, know that your eyes cannot remain dry. If trees are cut, you will not receive fruit, for giving fruit and shade is the duty of a tree. You are a part of society; understand yourself as a part, not its master. In this lies your welfare, and this knowledge is superior. The life of one who possesses this knowledge is itself a Yajna.Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you shall cross over all sin by the raft of knowledge alone.
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः |
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ||
Just as fire burns everything to ashes, so too the fire of knowledge burns the desire for the fruits of action, the anger that arises when fruits are not attained, and the delusion fostered by that anger, reducing them to ashes. O Pārtha, always remember this mantra: there is no purifier in this world like knowledge, nor is there any element superior to knowledge. Knowledge is supreme.
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते |
The ignorant, the faithless, the doubting soul perishes. Neither this world nor the next, nor happiness, is for the doubting soul.
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति |
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ||

O Krishna, Janardana! How can I fight against my own kinsmen, revered elders, and teachers like Bhishma and Drona, who stand before me? My heart is overwhelmed with grief at the thought of slaying them. What good is a kingdom gained by such a sin?

O Son of Kunti, these joys and sorrows are like the seasons; they come and go. He who remains steadfast and untroubled by both pleasure and pain, enduring them without being affected, is truly wise and fit for liberation.
मात्रास्पर्शास्तु कौंतेय शीतोष्णसुखदुःखदाः। आगमापायिनोऽनित्यास्तांस्तितिक्षस्व भारत।।
O Bharata, free yourself from the fear of killing or being killed, for death can only befall that which is born. The soul is beyond time, beyond even Kal. It is the body that is born, not the soul. If the soul does not take birth, how can it die? The soul simply is, O Partha. It exists on both shores of time and within its current. It is unborn, eternal, everlasting, ancient, and imperishable. Therefore, to be worried about killing or being killed is utterly futile, O Partha, utterly futile. Death only affects the body, and even after its demise, the soul does not die. For weapons cannot cleave it, fire cannot burn it, water cannot wet it, nor can wind dry it.
नैनं छिन्दन्ति शस्त्राणि नैनं दहति पावकः। न चैनं क्लेदयंत्यापो न शोषयति मारुतः।।
Now, what is it that troubles you, Partha?

But Janardana, why do I regard the soul as a father or a child? I used to seek the soul, wearing dusty clothes, while they (the elders) in their pure white garments stood before me. Is that elder, who taught me archery, merely a soul? Did that body, which you call the garment of the soul, not many times bless me by placing its hand on my head? Keshav, I do not deny the eternal, ancient, unborn, and imperishable nature of the soul. But I am speaking of these ancient शरीरों (bodies)! Do these bodies not also matter to me? The soul does not take birth, Keshav, the soul does not take birth! But these people take birth, do they not? Some people do take birth!

Yes, those people certainly take birth, O Partha. But push this thought a little further, O mighty-armed one, push it a little further. Whoever is born, their death is certain. So why grieve for what is certain? One who is born must die one day. And this death is not the end, because the one who dies will be reborn. This is an immutable truth, O Partha, and no one can avert this immutable truth – neither you, nor I, nor anyone else. Even Bhishma, the son of Ganga, possesses the boon of desired death, yet death ultimately comes to all who are born.

My limbs are trembling, my mouth is parched, and my bow Gandiva is slipping from my hand. I see no good in slaying my own kinsmen, O Keshava. I desire neither victory nor kingdom nor happiness, for what good are they if those for whom we desire them stand arrayed for battle? My heart is overwhelmed with the weakness of compassion, and my mind is bewildered about my duty. I cannot fight, O Govinda.

O Partha, how has this delusion and despondency come upon you at such a critical moment? It is un-Aryan, leads not to heaven, and is disgraceful.
कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम्।
अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन।। (भगवद गीता २.२)
Before you called my name, tell me, Partha, when the clouds of destruction surround us from all sides, and the protection of Dharma and victory look towards you, how have you allowed such feelings of cowardice to enter your heart in this hour of crisis? Superior men do not sink into such sorrow. In this decisive battle between Dharma and Adharma, do not be impotent, Partha, do not be impotent! O scorcher of foes, O Dhananjaya, this sentiment of yours is unworthy; it will cast you down from heaven and also from glory. You yourself will become the cause of your own disgrace. Therefore, O Partha, abandon this weakness of heart and stand up for battle!

How can I fight, O Madhusudana? How can I fight to kill my grandsire (Bhishma)? How can I fight to strike Dronacharya? How can I fight those who are venerable to me? My well-wishers have taught me a mantra to conquer me. How can I stand to conquer them? It is far better to live by spreading my hand for alms and eating the bread of beggary than to eat food stained with the blood of these great souls. I am also unable to understand whether victory or defeat is superior in this war. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before me like enemies. If I win, it will not be possible to live without killing them. O Keshava, even after killing them, life will not be desirable. Why? Because they are my brothers! O Keshava, what is your guidance?

You have only asked this, Partha. But this war is not for establishing or identifying relationships and kinsmen, O son of Kunti. Recognize your duty and then decide, because you alone will have to make the decision. If you wish that I make the decision and you escape the responsibility of this war, then that will not happen, Partha, never will it happen! Because this war is yours, and the outcome of this war will also be yours.

The path of duty is not clearly visible to me, Keshava. Therefore, Vasudeva, please become the charioteer of my soul as well. I know I stand between Dharma and Adharma, but I cannot decide which side is Dharma and which is Adharma. I seek your guidance and the way to escape this grief that drains my senses. In this mental state, I cannot fight, Govinda.
O Krishna, how can I fight against my own kin, my teachers, and elders? I see only sorrow and sin in this battle, even if I gain a kingdom. My mind is filled with doubt and despair.

O Partha, if you do not fight, not only will your enemies but society itself brand you a disgraced coward, and future generations will consider you timid and sinful. Therefore, O Mighty-armed one, do not dwell on questions of victory and defeat, life and death, pleasure and pain. Fight! For if you are victorious in this war, you will enjoy the kingdom of the earth and its glory; and if you attain valorous death, you will achieve fame and attain heaven. Therefore, O Son of Kunti, arise! Treat joy and sorrow, gain and loss, victory and defeat as equal, and fight. For this is both your Kshatriya duty and your human dharma. हतौ वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्। तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः॥ (Either slain, you will attain heaven, or victorious, you will enjoy the earth. Therefore, arise, O son of Kunti, determined to fight.) The soul does not die. Do not harbor this dilemma or confusion in your mind.
Govinda, I cannot do this! I am overcome with profound sorrow, my mind agitated and distressed. How can I fight?

Indeed, Partha. Those who are gone are gone. The wise grieve neither for those who are gone nor for those who are not. They do not sorrow for the past, nor for what is yet to come. Your words sound like those of the wise, yet you speak like the ignorant. Before you grieve, consider this: what you are grieving for is not worthy of grief.
Then, Keshav, are revered figures like my grandfather and my teachers not worthy of grief?

If they were truly worthy of such grief, I would tell you, O Bharata. Understand this truth, Partha: the fundamental essence is not the body, but the soul. Death is not the end of its journey, for its journey is infinite. Death is merely a stop, Partha, just a stop. The cessation of breath is not the cessation of the vital air. Understand, Partha, a being is first a child, then becomes a youth, then old, and then comes death. But this journey is of the body; the soul goes beyond even this. It casts off one body and takes on another. Therefore, the journey that ends with death is only the journey of the body, Partha, only the journey of the body.न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचित्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः।अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणोन हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे॥The soul's journey is eternal, Partha. At one point in its journey, the body is left behind, and the traveler moves on. And it wears a new body just as we cast off old clothes and put on new ones.वासांसि जीर्णानि यथा विहाय नवानि गृह्णाति नरोऽपराणि।तथा शरीराणि विहाय जीर्णान्य् अन्यानि संयाति नवानि देही॥Destruction, Partha, cannot touch the soul. So why lament the destruction of anything? Is it for the destruction of clothes? But clothes are not truly 'ours'; they are meant to be cast off. And the soul never dies, never. Even those standing before you, after this war, will all be gone.What is this 'being' and 'not being,' Partha? For there was never a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these people. And there will never be a time in the future when I shall cease to be, nor you, nor all these people. Why, then, Partha, are you caught in the illusion that the present life is the complete life? The present life is not the complete life, Partha. We were, we are, and we shall be.

O Keshav, as I look upon my kinsmen, teachers, and elders arrayed before me, my heart is filled with sorrow and confusion. I am uncertain of my duty, my dharma. What should I do in this situation? What is my true dharma?

Why then, O Partha, is there room for lamentation in this endless cycle of birth, death, and rebirth? Those whom you see before you, O Partha, existed before this birth, though you did not know it. They will exist after this birth, though you will not know what form they take. Their existence truly lies beyond these two points of birth and death, or if it does, it remains unmanifest and unknown to you. Therefore, O Partha, when death is an inevitable part of life, an end that you can neither prevent nor alter, why do you grieve? Why lament? You knew neither your grandsire, your teachers, nor these relatives before this birth, nor will you know them after it. To grieve for them is futile. All beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest in the middle state, and unmanifest again after death. What is there to lament?
अव्यक्तादीनि भूतानि व्यक्तमध्यानि भारत। अव्यक्तनिधनान्येव तत्र का परिदेवना॥
What is there to be amazed by, O Partha? Just as discarding worn-out clothes is the ultimate truth for garments, so is death the ultimate truth for the body. Why then grieve for the truth? This human body and soul are not a mixture of perishable and imperishable; the body is merely an instrument of the soul. Therefore, without worrying about the body, one should continue to perform one's dharma. However, even if you consider your Kshatriya dharma, O Partha, you should not waver. For a warrior, there is no greater good than a righteous war.
स्वधर्ममपि चावेक्ष्य न विकम्पितुमर्हसि। धर्म्याद्धि युद्धात् क्षत्रियस्य न विद्यतेऽन्यत्श्रेयः॥
It is the dharma of a Kshatriya to take up arms against unrighteousness, and those who stand against dharma are before you. Therefore, O Partha, fulfill your Kshatriya dharma. But tell me, O Partha, who are you? Who do you consider yourself to be?
I am Arjuna, the disciple of Drona. I am Arjuna, the son of Kunti. And, O Keshav, I am a Kshatriya.

If you were merely a Kshatriya, O Partha, you would not be Drona's disciple. And even as Kunti's son, you are a Kshatriya. All your identities are those of a Kshatriya. Therefore, Kshatriya dharma is your dharma; fulfill it. Wielding weapons against adharma is the Kshatriya dharma. Taking up arms against injustice and unrighteousness is the Kshatriya dharma. And if, in this decisive moment, you do not take up arms in favor of truth and against untruth, O Partha, you will fail your dharma.
O Krishna, I observe the world filled with actions and their consequences. How can one act and yet remain untouched by the fruits of those actions? How can one truly be free from the bonds of karma?

Look at me, Partha. I have indeed created this society and its divisions based on qualities and actions. Yet, I have never desired the fruits of this creation. Therefore, even though I am the doer, I am not the doer. One who understands this secret, Partha, will never be entangled in their actions. My actions do not bind me, nor do I have any desire for the fruits of action. It is because I have no desire for the fruits of action that actions do not contaminate me. You too, Partha, perform desireless actions and do not let the shadow of your selfish interests fall upon your deeds.
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥
O Bharata, you speak of Karma. Please explain, what is the difference between Karma, Akarma, and Vikarma?

O Bharata, understand this distinction. Karma is action, but that action performed without the expectation of results is Akarma. And actions that are not for the benefit of the individual or society are Vikarma; they are forbidden. Action is superior, and the doer who is free from the desire for the fruits of action is even more superior. Partha, the one who is a non-doer (Akarta), who is free from the desire for the fruits of action, he alone is wise, intelligent, and a Karma Yogi. For him, his action itself is the fruit of action, and therefore, after performing one action, he does not wait for its result but moves on to the next. The fire of his knowledge burns away the impurities of attachment, anger, hatred, desire, gain-loss, joy-sorrow, purifying his actions. Thus, his action becomes Akarma, and he transforms from a doer to a non-doer (Akarta). This wise non-doer does nothing for himself other than acquiring the necessary means of livelihood; his remaining actions are for the welfare of society. This person, even while performing actions, is not tainted by sin; his life itself becomes beneficial for society. The life of such a person is a Yajna (sacrifice). You too, make your life a Yajna, and in its sacrificial fire, burn your desire for the fruits of action, attachment, and anger like offerings.
O Krishna, what is the purpose of Your advent? Why do You manifest Yourself in this world, and what is truly superior within us that can help us overcome our struggles?

My dear Arjuna, I appear in this world to protect the righteous, annihilate the wicked, and re-establish the principles of Dharma. I manifest Myself millennium after millennium. परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्। धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे॥ Furthermore, know this, O Partha: The senses are superior to inert matter, and the mind is superior to the senses. Superior to the mind is the intellect, and even superior to the intellect is the soul. इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः। मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः॥ Therefore, O Partha, focus your attention on the soul. Strive to rise above the body, the senses, the mind, and the intellect.
O Krishna, I am tormented by the thought of fighting my own relatives. What is the true nature of action, and how can I avoid sin by engaging in such a terrible war?

O Bhārata, even the ignorant perform actions, but only with a view to their own self-interest. The action of the wise, however, is selfless; it is for maintaining the balance of the world, for universal welfare. Therefore, O Pārtha, do not bear any burden on your mind; offer your actions to Me and fight this righteous war. On the path of performing one's duty, even death becomes auspicious. If you have to slay even your grandsires, teachers, and relatives, you will still incur no sin, for the performance of duty is free from sin, O Pārtha, the performance of duty is free from sin. If they attain valorous death, their demise will be auspicious, and if you attain valorous death, your demise will also be auspicious. Therefore, O Pārtha, fight! For the path of Dharma cannot be the path of sin.

O Krishna, I strive to understand this path of duty. Yet, I see many individuals, and sometimes even myself, becoming entangled in worldly desires and emotions, leading to distress. What causes a person's downfall, and how does one lose their peace of mind?

O Pārtha, a common man contemplates sense objects, and this contemplation makes him attached to them.
ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते।
सङ्गात्सञ्जायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥
क्रोधाद्भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः।
स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति॥
From this attachment, desire is born. When desire is unfulfilled, anger arises. From anger comes delusion, from delusion loss of memory, from loss of memory destruction of intelligence, and from destruction of intelligence, he perishes. O son of Kuntī, your current delusion is leading you towards the destruction of your intelligence. Just think, O Pārtha, how can one without intellect find peace? Such a person cannot even differentiate between peace and disturbance. How can one who cannot distinguish peace from disturbance ever be happy? O Pārtha, just as gales shake a boat, so do desires distract the intellect.
O Krishna, your words enlighten me on the perils of attachment. But if one knows the path of Dharma, what force compels a person, even against their own will, to commit sinful acts?

O Pārtha, if this topic has come up, then know that sometimes a person becomes so inclined to commit sin. What compels him? His lust compels him, his self-interest compels him, his anger, his delusion compel him. Identify these enemies, O Pārtha. Just as smoke covers fire, or dust covers a mirror, or the amnion covers an embryo, so do lust, delusion, and desire cover knowledge.
आवृतं ज्ञानमेतेन ज्ञानिनो नित्यवैरिणा।
कामरूपेण कौन्तेय दुष्पूरेणानलेन च॥
This insatiable, destructive form of desire and anger, the eternal enemy of the wise, covers knowledge. Therefore, O son of Kuntī, these destroy the knowledge of the wise.
O Keshav, what is the path to truly purify oneself and attain wisdom?
Arjuna, cleanse your heart like fire purifies gold, purify your intellect like cleaning a mirror, and by controlling your senses, slay the destroyers of knowledge and discrimination.
But O Keshav, why is Dharma harmed?

Dharma is harmed, Partha, because humanity fails to break the bonds of attachment. One cannot break ties with their own self to connect with society. If it were not so, then the Lakshagraha incident would not have occurred, Draupadi's disrobing would not have happened, and the Kaurava and Pandava armies would not be standing facing each other today.
Then, when Draupadi was disrobed, should I not harbor personal anger or seek retribution for it?

Partha, this decision is yours alone. However, Draupadi's disrobing is not merely your personal problem. A society that remained silent when Draupadi, the Empress of Indraprastha, daughter of King Drupada, and wife of the Pandavas, was dishonored, how can that society protect the honor of any ordinary woman? Draupadi's disrobing is a social problem, Partha, a social problem. It is your duty to wage war to destroy those forces that can dishonor any Draupadi. These forces are enemies of society, Partha. Therefore, do not hesitate to fight even those great warriors who have come to side with these evil forces. Free yourself from the bonds of personal anger and attachment, and fight for the welfare of the world, Partha. This is your supreme duty. Yes, Partha, you are My devotee and also My friend. Therefore, I am going to reveal to you that Yoga which has long been lost. At the beginning of creation, I Myself imparted it to Surya, and from Surya, it passed to Manu, and from Manu, it reached Ikshvaku.
You gave it to Surya? But O Keshav, you have taken birth in this modern age, and Surya Dev is ancient. How can I believe that at the beginning of creation, you gave this Yoga to Surya Dev?

बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन। तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परंतप॥ Yes, Partha, many births of Mine and yours have passed. I remember all of them, but you do not, O scorcher of foes. Though I am unborn, imperishable, and the Lord of all beings, I manifest Myself by subjugating My own material nature through My Yoga-maya. यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत। अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥ परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्। धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे॥ Yes, Partha, I manifest. I come whenever Dharma declines, O Bharata; and whenever adharma (unrighteousness) prevails, I then manifest Myself. To protect the righteous, to annihilate the wicked, and to re-establish Dharma, I manifest Myself from age to age.
O Krishna, I find myself entangled in this material existence, filled with doubts and sorrow. What is the true nature of this world that binds us, and how can one ever transcend it?

Arjuna, this world is like an inverted tree, whose roots extend deeply into human society, nourished by the three qualities of nature – sattva, rajas, and tamas. Its actual form, its beginning, end, and its foundation cannot be perceived in this material world. However, a person can cut down this tree of worldly existence with the axe of detachment, or vairagya, and attain that supreme abode from which there is no return. And, O Partha, detachment is simply the renunciation of desires.
Krishna, understanding the need for detachment, how then can I achieve it amidst these overwhelming duties and the turmoil I face? What is the path to truly surrender and find that supreme abode?

Therefore, if you must think, think only of Me. If you must ask, ask only Me. Offer yourself to Me, O best of archers, and come to My refuge. I shall free you from all sins.मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मेPlace your mind on Me, O Partha, become My devotee, and offer your obeisances to Me. If you do so, I promise you, you will certainly attain Me, for you are very dear to Me.सर्वधर्मान्परित्यज्य मामेकं शरणं व्रज अहम् त्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मोक्षयिष्यामि मा शुचःAbandon all varieties of dharmas and simply surrender unto Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sinful reactions; do not fear. Therefore, do not grieve, Arjuna, do not grieve, O dear devotee. I am the ultimate point and supreme goal of Karma Yoga, Bhakti Yoga, and Jnana Yoga. Therefore, act without attachment like a Yogi. Do not worry, O Partha, do not worry. Have faith in Me. O mighty-armed, pick up your Gandiva and fight!
What is Yoga, O Krishna? What does the term 'Yoga' truly mean?

O Partha, I was just telling you. Yoga is skill in action. It is the skill of renouncing attachment, the skill of performing one's duty without attachment. It is the ability to remain equanimous in both success and failure.बुद्धियुक्तो जहातीह उभे सुकृतदुष्कृते। तस्माद्योगाय युज्यस्व योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्॥A person endowed with wisdom discards both good and evil deeds in this life. Therefore, strive for Yoga, for Yoga is skill in action.
How then, O Krishna, can I recognize a sage of steady wisdom (स्थितप्रज्ञ)? What are their characteristics? How does such a one speak?

There is no difficulty in recognizing such a one, O Partha.प्रजहाति यदा कामान् सर्वान् पार्थ मनोगतान्। आत्मन्येवात्मना तुष्टः स्थितप्रज्ञस्तदोच्यते॥When one completely casts away all desires of the mind, O Partha, and is content in the Self by the Self alone, then one is called a person of steady wisdom.Like that, you too should abandon your desires and be free from personal ambitions. Be satisfied in yourself, beyond joy and sorrow. Then neither the fire of sorrow will burn you, nor the rain of happiness will drench you.The sage of steady wisdom maintains equanimity in both joy and sorrow, and no one can disturb this balance. When their words emerge, they do not come from the fluctuating mind, but from the unfathomable depths of the soul. They do not speak the language of Brahman, but the language of selfless action. When such a one sits, they withdraw into themselves like a tortoise, making their inner self a fortress. This means their senses are completely under their control, and only one whose own mind is under control can master their senses.
What, then, are the obstacles, O Krishna, that prevent one from attaining such steady wisdom and controlling their senses?

O Partha, a common person dwells on the objects of the senses, and this contemplation makes them attached. From this attachment, desire is born. When desire is unfulfilled, anger arises. When anger arises, attachment to the object increases further.ध्यायतो विषयान् पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते। सङ्गात् सञ्जायते कामः कामात् क्रोधोऽभिजायते॥ क्रोधाद् भवति सम्मोहः सम्मोहात् स्मृतिविभ्रमः। स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात् प्रणश्यति॥While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment to them; from attachment, desire is born; from desire, anger arises. From anger, delusion arises; from delusion, the loss of memory; from the loss of memory, the destruction of intelligence; from the destruction of intelligence, one perishes.And when that delusion increases, O Partha, the power of thought deviates. When the power of thought deviates, intelligence is destroyed, and when intelligence is destroyed, a person is completely ruined. O son of Kunti, your current delusion is leading you towards the destruction of your intelligence.Just consider, O Partha, how can one who has no intelligence attain peace? Such a one cannot even differentiate between peace and restlessness. And how can one who cannot distinguish between peace and restlessness ever be happy?Just as a strong wind can carry away a boat on the water, O Partha, so do desires mislead the intelligence.इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते। तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि॥For, the mind which yields to the wandering senses carries away one's wisdom, just as a gale carries away a boat on the water.
Keshav, I still do not understand what benefit this war will bring.

Dhananjaya, gain and loss are both relative terms. I know that you do not desire the enjoyments of this earth or the pleasures of heaven. Therefore, you must rise above these dualities: सुख-दुःखे समे कृत्वा लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ। ततो युद्धाय युज्यस्व नैवं पापमवाप्स्यसि।। Treating alike pleasure and pain, gain and loss, victory and defeat, engage yourself in battle for the sake of battle; thus you will not incur sin, Partha.
But I still cannot rise above them, Keshav. How can I?

Partha, until now I have been explaining to you from the perspective of knowledge and wisdom, which can see through life and understand the truth by delving into its essence. But perhaps you are entangled in its abstraction. Then, look at this moment from the perspective of practical action, Partha. If you decide on your duty from the perspective of practical action, you will still arrive at the conclusion that it is necessary for you to participate in this war.
This is the very decision I am unable to make, Keshav. Why am I unable to make it?

You are unable to make this decision, Partha, only because you are weighing this moment solely in terms of personal gain and personal loss. This is the bondage of attachment (moha), Partha. This is the root of your sorrow. And that is why this cowardly, destructive, and disgraceful grief of yours is neither in your interest nor in that of society.
Keshav, you say that wisdom is paramount, superior to action. Then why do you urge me to engage in this bloody conflict? Why should I fight? I seek the path to welfare; please guide me, Keshav.

Arjuna, there are two paths proclaimed in this world, O sinless one: the path of knowledge for the contemplative, and the path of action for the active.
लोकेऽस्मिन् द्विविधा निष्ठा पुरा प्रोक्ता मयानघ ज्ञानयोगेन साङ्ख्यानां कर्मयोगेन योगिनाम्
There are two kinds of people in this world: introverted and extroverted. Those who are introverted seek God within themselves; this is Gyan Yoga. Those who are extroverted try to attain Him by moving outside themselves. But you cannot escape action, for even searching within oneself is an action. O son of Kunti, these are the two paths: one of Gyan Yoga and the other of Karma Yoga.
Then, Keshav, why should I not simply follow the path of Gyan Yoga?

But, Arjuna, Gyan Yoga is not the path of abandoning action, nor is it the path to perfection without action. For life itself is impossible without action. If there are eyes, they will surely see; if there are eyelids, they will surely blink; if there are ears, they will surely hear. One who forcibly restrains the organs of action and then contemplates on the objects of the senses is neither a Yogi nor a truly wise person; he is a hypocrite. The perfect person controls their senses; they do not suppress them, Arjuna. They do not live with their eyes closed. Without action, the journey of the body is not possible. A person will breathe, won't they, Arjuna? If there is a scent or a foul smell in the environment, they are compelled to experience it. If there is a sound, a noise, a clamor around them, their ears will not wait for their command to hear it. Therefore, one who controls their senses, who places the bridle of their consciousness upon them and directs them to act, who shows them the direction of action – that person is superior. They understand their choices, Arjuna, and use their willpower. And, Arjuna, performing one's prescribed duties is better than not doing anything. It is also true, Arjuna, that eyes see, but what they should see and what they should not see – that decision is made by the wise person themselves. They do not give free rein to hands to see, to ears to hear, or to feet to walk. At such a crossroads of choices stand the wise and the ignorant.

O Krishna, you are the Supreme Brahman, the purest, the eternal, the divine essence. You are God, the unborn. O Giridhar, only you truly know yourself. How can I, O embodiment of divine knowledge, truly know and recognize you? Please describe your glories to me in detail, O Madhava.

O best among gurus, there is no end to My divine manifestations. Yet, listen. I am the Self, seated in the hearts of all beings. अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः। अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च॥ O Gudakesha, I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings. Among the Adityas, I am Vishnu; among the Maruts, Marichi; among the luminaries, the Sun, and among the constellations, the Moon. वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि देवानामस्मि वासवाः। इन्द्रियाणां मनश्चास्मि भूतानामस्मि चेतना॥ Among the Vedas, I am the Sama Veda; among the gods, Indra; among the senses, the mind; and among living beings, consciousness. Among the Rudras, I am Shankara; among Yakshas and Rakshasas, Kubera; among Vasus, Agni; and among mountains, Meru. Among priests, I am Brihaspati; among generals, Kartikeya; and among reservoirs, the ocean. Among great sages, I am Bhrigu; among words, Om; among sacrifices, Japa Yajna; and among immovable things, the Himalayas. Among trees, I am the Ashvattha (Pipal); and among divine sages, Narada. Among Gandharvas, I am Chitraratha; and among Siddhas, Kapila Muni. O great warrior, among horses, know Me as Uchchaishrava, born of nectar; among elephants, Airavata; and among humans, the king. Among weapons, I am the thunderbolt; among cows, Kamadhenu; among procreators, Kama (Cupid); and among serpents, Vasuki (Shesha Naga). प्रह्लादश्चास्मि दैत्यानां कालः कलयतामहम्। मृगाणां च मृगेन्द्रोऽहं वैनतेयश्च पक्षिणाम्॥ Among Daityas, I am Prahlada; among reckoners, I am Time; among beasts, I am the lion; and among birds, I am Garuda. And among wielders of weapons, I am Rama. Among letters, I am 'A'; I am never-ending Time. I am all-devouring death, O Partha, and I am the origin of all those who are yet to be born in the coming years and whose beginning has not yet begun. मृत्युः सर्वहरश्चाहमुद्भवश्च भविष्यताम्। कीर्तिः श्रीर्वाक् च नारीणां स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः क्षमा॥ Among women, I am fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, fortitude, and forgiveness. I am gambling of the cunning, and the splendor of the splendid. I am goodness, victory, endeavor. Among Yadavas, I am Vasudeva; and among Pandavas, Arjuna. Among sages, I am Vyasa; and among poets, Ushana (Shukracharya). यच्चापि सर्वभूतानां बीजं तदहमर्जुन। न तदस्ति विना यत्स्यान्मया भूतं चराचरम्॥ And whatever is the seed of all beings, that am I, O Arjuna. There is no being, moving or non-moving, that exists without Me. I am indeed the seed of creation, O Partha.
Krishna, what causes the decline of Dharma and the rise of unrighteousness in the world?

Whenever there is a decline of righteousness (Dharma) and a rise of unrighteousness (Adharma), I manifest Myself. I come for the protection of the good, the destruction of the wicked, and the re-establishment of Dharma. Dharma declines, O Partha, because humans fail to transcend the bonds of attachment (moh). They sever their connection with their true self and thus fail to connect with society. If this were not the case, O Partha, the Lakshagriha incident would not have occurred, Draupadi would not have been disrobed, and the armies of the Kauravas and Pandavas would not stand arrayed against each other.
Should I not then feel anger over Draupadi's disrobing?

That decision, O Partha, you must make for yourself. However, Draupadi's disrobing is not merely your personal problem. What respect for an ordinary woman's honor can a society uphold, if it silently watches the disrobing of Draupadi – the Empress of Indraprastha, daughter of King Drupada, and wife of the Pandavas? Draupadi's disrobing is a societal problem, Partha. It is your duty to wage war to destroy those powers capable of disrobing any Draupadi. These powers are enemies of society. And do not hesitate to fight even those great personalities who have come to this war to support those powers. Free yourself from the bonds of personal anger and attachment, and fight for the welfare of the world, Partha. This is your supreme duty.
How can one act, Lord, without desiring the fruits of action, especially when one is the doer? You, the creator, act without attachment to results. What is the path to such liberation from karma?

Look at Me, Partha. I Myself have created this society and its divisions based on qualities (gunas) and actions (karmas). Yet, I have never desired the fruits of this social creation. Thus, though I am the doer, I am also the non-doer. And he who understands this secret, Partha, will never be bound by his actions.न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा।इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते॥ (Bhagavad Gita 4.14)Actions do not contaminate Me; I have no desire for the fruits of action. One who understands this truth about Me is also not entangled by actions. Since I have no desire for the fruits of action, actions do not defile Me. You too, Partha, perform actions without desire for results, and do not let the shadow of your self-interest fall upon your actions.
O Bharata, what is the difference between Karma, Akarma, and Vikarma?

Understand the difference between Karma, Akarma, and Vikarma, O Partha. Karma is action. But an action performed without the expectation of its fruits is Akarma. And an action that is not beneficial to the individual or society is Vikarma, it is forbidden. Akarma is superior. He who is a non-doer, who is free from the desire for the fruits of action, he alone is truly knowledgeable, intelligent, and a Karma Yogi. For him, his action itself is the fruit of action.
Krishna, what is the true nature of action and duty? How can one find welfare and liberation without getting entangled in the complexities of the world?

Arjuna, your body is transient; therefore, do not strive to escape your actions (karma). Your selfless action (nishkam karma) is your true duty and dharma. However, if your actions are solely for your own benefit, that path leads to sin. Therefore, free yourself from attachment and become a 'Karmaveer' (hero of action) for the welfare of society. This alone is the path to liberation, for all other actions are bound by attachment, illusion, and anger, and bind the self. Only actions performed selflessly will lead you on the path to liberation. If society is not happy, an individual cannot remain happy. If there are tears in society's eyes, understand that your eyes cannot remain dry. If trees are uprooted, you too will find no shade, because giving fruits and shade is the duty of a tree. You are a part of society; understand yourself as a part, not its master. In this lies your welfare, and this knowledge is supreme. One who possesses this knowledge leads a life of Yajna (sacrifice). Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you shall cross over all sin by the raft of knowledge.
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं संतरिष्यसि।।
Understand that just as fire reduces everything to ashes, so too does the fire of knowledge burn away the anger that arises from not achieving desired results, and all subsequent actions driven by such anger. Partha, always remember this mantra: In this world, there is nothing as purifying as knowledge, nor any other essence. Knowledge is supreme. One who is ignorant, who lacks faith, and who is full of doubt, perishes. He finds no happiness in this world, nor in the next.
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः।।
Therefore, O Bharata, abandon doubt and awaken the sage within you. Become a Gyana Yogi (Yogi of Knowledge), Partha, become a Gyana Yogi! And understand that the pinnacle of knowledge is Karma Sanyasa (renunciation of action).
Krishna, you praise both Karma Sanyasa and Karma Yoga (the path of action). How can this be, as they seem contradictory?

My friend, they do not contradict each other; both are benevolent and lead to welfare. However, among the two, Karma Yoga is superior. How so? One who works without aversion and desire is indeed a perpetual renunciate (Nitya Sanyasi). Such a person, free from both, is liberated from worldly bondage. Therefore, one who considers Karma Sanyasa and Karma Yoga as separate is foolish. The wise never think so. The renunciation of action (Karma Tyaga) is truly the abandonment of inherent self-interest along the path, Partha. Hence, the attainment of Karma Sanyasa is impossible without Karma Yoga. A Karma Yogi understands the fundamental truths, and his seeing and not seeing, hearing and not hearing, tasting and not tasting, waking and not waking, taking and not taking, giving up and not giving up—and every action of his—is for the welfare of the world.
O Keshava, how does a Yogi overcome his sorrows? The mind is restless; how can it be restrained and brought under the control of the Self? And who is considered the supreme among such Yogis?

O Partha, just as the flame of a lamp remains steady in a windless place, so too does the mind of a Yogi, free from desire, become unwavering, and his sorrows are dispelled. Let the restless mind indulge its whims, but you must restrain it and make it subservient to your Self. This is the remedy for you and others. Look towards Me, Partha; one who sees only Me in every direction and in every object can never stray. One who never forgets Me, I also never forget. Even while living a worldly life, such a person remains separate from the world and resides within Me. O Arjuna, the Yogi who regards the joy and sorrow of all beings as his own joy and sorrow, he indeed is considered the supreme. आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन। सुखं वा यदि वा दुःखं स योगी परमो मतः॥

But Keshava, can't the mind stray while walking the path of Yoga? It can certainly stray! If so, what is the consequence of this straying on the path to realizing Brahman? Does one who strays not become scattered and perish like a cloud?

No, Partha, one who strays does not become scattered and perish like a cloud. Whether in this world or the next, those who perform benevolent, auspicious deeds can never come to grief. Fix your mind on Me, perform Yoga depending solely on Me. You will attain My complete, doubt-free knowledge.
O Keshava, who are You, that I should fix my mind upon You and whose doubt-free perfect knowledge shall I attain? Please describe Your true nature.

O Dhananjaya, the greatest truth is I alone. I am the thread on which all this creation is strung like pearls. I am the taste in water, I am the light in the sun and moon, I am the Om in the Vedas, I am the sound in the ether. I am the sacred fragrance in the earth, I am the vigor in fire, I am the life force in all beings, I am the penance of ascetics. O Partha, I am the primal seed, I am the intelligence of the intelligent, I am the splendor of the splendid, I am the strength of the strong, free from desire, and I am that desire in beings which is not contrary to Dharma. I am in everything, Partha, yet I am distinct from all. I am unborn, I am without attributes. O Partha, I know all beings of the past, this present time, and all future times, but no one truly knows Me. I am the father of the universe, the mother, and the sustainer. I am the Rig Veda and I am the Sama Veda. I am the Lord and I am the refuge. I am creation and I am dissolution. I am the support of all, Partha! I am everything, everything. I am immortality and death, and I am the rain that falls and that which holds it back. And O Partha, I am also the imperishable seed of this world. I am the dearest friend of all, yet I am impartial to all. No one is dear to Me, nor is anyone hateful. But those who worship Me with devotion, My friend, they are in Me, and I am in them.

O Krishna, my mind is assailed by doubt. All actions, it seems, lead to entanglement and suffering in this material world. Is it not more prudent to renounce all action in the pursuit of liberation and lasting peace? What, then, is the truly righteous path I should embrace?

Indeed, Arjuna, your perception is incomplete. Understand that action (karma) is essential; without it, the very sustenance of the body is impossible. As it is said: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो हि अकर्मणः। शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्धयेदकर्मणः॥ (Bhagavad Gita 3.8) (Perform your prescribed duties, for action is superior to inaction. Even the maintenance of your physical body would not be possible without work.) Therefore, act, but act like a wise person. Perform your actions as a sacrifice (Yajna). यज्ञार्थात्कर्मणोऽन्यत्र लोकोऽयं कर्मबन्धनः। तदर्थं कर्म कौन्तेय मुक्तसङ्गः समाचर॥ (Bhagavad Gita 3.9) (Work performed as a sacrifice for Vishnu has to be performed, otherwise work is the cause of bondage in this material world. Therefore, O son of Kunti, perform your prescribed duties for His satisfaction, and in that way you will always remain free from bondage.) Know that karma itself is Yajna, and its source is the imperishable Brahman; thus, the path of action directly leads to the Divine. One whose life does not contribute to the cycle of creation lives a life devoid of value. Do not fall into this worthlessness. He who thinks only of his personal problems is a sinner. Therefore, emerge from this web of illusion, recognize your duties, and fulfill them, Arjuna. The desire for the fruits of action is the true impediment on your path. It is like a stone tied around a person’s neck, preventing them from rising above their lower self. This very desire isolates an individual from society, pushing them into the mire of personal gain and loss. Remember, Arjuna, society is not in you; you are in society. Therefore, consider the welfare of the world (Lokasangraha) and the public good as your supreme duty. What is beneficial for society will ultimately be beneficial for you. Perfection will be attained through actions performed for Lokasangraha, for the path of personal gain only leads to sin, diverting one for selfish motives. Furthermore, do not forget, Arjuna, that you are a great soul. People will regard you as an example and follow you on the path of desire and self-interest, for the conduct of a superior person becomes a standard for others. Consider My own example: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन। नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यं वर्त एव च कर्मणि॥ (Bhagavad Gita 3.22) (O son of Pritha, there is no work prescribed for Me within all the three planetary systems—nor am I in want of anything, nor have I a need to obtain anything—and yet I am engaged in prescribed duties.) I am here before you, performing actions, demonstrating and proving that it is possible to live a life while treading the path of desireless action. सक्ताः कर्मण्यविद्वांसो यथा कुर्वन्ति भारत। कुर्याद्विद्वांस्तथासक्तश्चिकीर्षुर्लोकसंग्रहम्॥ (Bhagavad Gita 3.25) (As the ignorant perform their duties with attachment to the results, so should the learned act without attachment, desiring the welfare of the world, O son of Bharata.) The ignorant perform actions driven by their inherent self-interest. The wise, however, act selflessly, for the welfare of the world, to maintain the balance of existence. Therefore, O Arjuna, do not bear any burden on your mind. Offer your actions to Me, perform this righteous duty, and steadfastly follow the path of your obligations.

My eyes have been opened; the clouds of doubt and apprehension have dispersed. What You have said is the truth, and there is no other truth besides it. However, O Supreme Lord, today I wish to behold Your divine form!

O sinless Arjuna, you cannot see My true form with these mortal eyes. For this, you will require divine vision. न तु मां शक्यसे द्रष्टुमनेनैव स्वचक्षुषा। दिव्यं ददामि ते चक्षुः पश्य मे योगमैश्वरम्॥ (Bhagavad Gita 11.8) But you cannot see Me with your ordinary eyes. Therefore, I give you divine vision. Behold My mystic opulence!

अदृष्टपूर्वं हृषितोऽस्मि दृष्ट्वा भयेन च प्रव्यथितं मनो मे। तदेव मे दर्शय देवरूपं प्रसीद देवेश जगन्निवास॥ (Bhagavad Gita 11.45) O Devesh, Jagannivas, having seen this wondrous, cosmic form of Yours, which was never seen before, I am thrilled with joy, yet my mind is greatly perturbed with fear! Therefore, please be gracious unto me and again show me Your divine human form. O Lord, O Vishvamurti, O Ananta, O Narayana, O Ocean of Mercy, please forgive me, just as a friend forgives a friend, a father forgives a son, and a Lord forgives His devotee. Please, forgive me, Lord, forgive me!

O son of Kunti, there is no place for forgiveness between a friend and a friend, a father and a son, or between God and His devotee. The basis of these relationships is faith (श्रद्धा) and devotion (भक्ति). मयी आवेश्य मनो ये मां नित्ययुक्ता उपासते। श्रद्धया परयोपेतास्ते मे युक्ततमा मताः॥ (Bhagavad Gita 12.2) One who fixes his mind on Me, who is always engaged in My devotion, who worships Me with great and transcendental faith, is considered by Me to be the most perfect yogi. Therefore, O Partha, My devotion is supreme. Those who are My devotees do not get entangled in this material world.
